title: When is the cleanest, and the cheapest, time to use electricity? Carbon intensity, prices, load shifting and storage on the GB grid, 2019–2025 (code, results and working paper)
description:
Code, processed results and working paper (version 1.0) for a study of when electricity use in Great Britain is cleanest and cheapest, 2019–2025, with an out-of-period check on January–October 2026.

Using public half-hourly data (NESO Carbon Intensity API; Elexon FUELHH generation and MID wholesale prices; Octopus Agile household prices), the study measures how the daily shape of carbon intensity and prices has changed, simulates flexible demand under fixed, forecast-based and price-based schedules (testing fixed rules out of sample), compares carbon and cost savings on the same days, and estimates the implied abatement cost of carbon-aware over cheapest scheduling. Version 1.0 adds a battery storage model (a daily linear programme comparing price-driven, carbon-driven and fixed-timer operation, at grid and household scale) and checks the main patterns on January–October 2026 data without re-fitting any rule. Marginal emission factors are estimated as a robustness check.

See README.md to reproduce the analysis.
